"Poor water quality and densely built riverbanks: otters were long considered extinct in Berlin. Since the 1960s they've been under strict protection, and since the 1990s their numbers have been rising again. In the 18th and 19th centuries they were heavily hunted, seen as competitors for food and prized for their fur. In recent years, thanks to wildlife and nature conservation, their population has recovered and they've increasingly been spotted in eastern Berlin. The modern urban environment, however, still poses many dangers for otters."
